system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

exchanges.user:
ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
The Seller’s characterisations of positions as “agreed”, “settled”, “adequate” or ordinary course are assertions only and do not establish Buyer approval.

| Ref. | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | Starting cap of **25% / AUD 6m**. The 20% fallback requires Amelia Frost’s prior written approval identifying this draft; none exists. | **Reject and mark up to AUD 6m (25%)** — the proposed fallback is not authorised merely because its number matches the playbook fallback. |
| **SPA-N-002 De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 deductible basket, with only excess recoverable. | **AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 tipping basket**, with Seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded. | **Reject and restore Buyer thresholds** — Seller’s thresholds materially suppress recovery and improperly convert the basket to a deductible. |
| **SPA-N-003 General claims time limit** | General claims notified within **18 months**. | **24 months after Completion**; 18 months requires Amelia Frost’s prior written approval, which has not been given. | **Reject and require 24 months** — the shorter fallback is unauthorised for this draft. |
| **SPA-N-004 Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title subject to the same cap and time limit as general warranties. | Separate regime with **100% cap**, at least **six years**, and no general basket, de minimis or knowledge bar. | **Reject entirely and create a separate Fundamental/Title regime** — ownership, authority and capacity risks cannot be diluted by general warranty limitations. |
| **SPA-N-005 Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims; no effective fraud carve-out is stated. | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of **all caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance**, to the maximum extent enforceable. | **Insert an express overriding carve-out** — this protection is mandatory under the playbook and cannot be waived. |
| **SPA-N-006 Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the entire data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public records. | Only **specific, fair disclosure**, with enough detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter; no deemed disclosure from bulk materials or prudent searches. | **Delete general/deemed disclosure and require warranty-specific disclosures** — wholesale incorporation does not fairly disclose exceptions to warranties. |
| **SPA-N-007 Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by Buyer or advisers, including anything discoverable in the data room or public records. | Delete the blanket exclusion and all constructive/imputed knowledge; any permitted knowledge mechanism must be tightly defined and must not affect title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. Seller warranty knowledge qualifiers should identify named Seller persons and require reasonable enquiry. | **Delete and resist any “discoverable” standard** — it shifts disclosure and diligence risk improperly to Buyer and its advisers. |
| **SPA-N-008 Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent, despite no final consent or evidence that clause 11.3 conditions are met. | A Completion condition requiring **effective Bluefen consent and evidence that all associated conditions have been satisfied** before Completion. | **Strengthen the condition and prohibit consent-on-delivery satisfaction** — Bluefen represents about 30% of FY26 revenue and incomplete/conditional consent is inadequate. |
| **SPA-N-009 Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m outstanding; security release to follow Completion. No final discharge is supplied. | Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective releases of all security at Completion. Any post-Completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost’s approval. | **Require payout and releases through the Completion mechanics** — Buyer should not acquire the company while Seller financing or security remains outstanding. |
| **SPA-N-010 Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses are said to be a Seller matter but are omitted from funds flow; on-costs are unaddressed. | Express Seller funding or a specific Completion line item for **AUD 420,000 plus triggered payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs**. | **Add an itemised Seller-funded amount and verify on-costs** — omission risks the Company/Buyer bearing a Completion-triggered Seller liability. |
| **SPA-N-011 Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; AUD 180,000 is recorded as open but not independently verified. | Broader indemnity covering payment, ownership/transfer, infringement and losses arising from failure to obtain the Project Materials, while preserving the SOW3 payment-and-assignment cure. Verify the payment amount/status. | **Broaden the indemnity and require payment/assignment evidence** — payment alone may not cure all chain-of-title and exploitation risks, and AUD 180,000 is unverified. |
| **SPA-N-012 Export/privacy incident** | Described as preliminary and not expected to be material; no confirmed access, breach, notification duty or loss. | Preservation of logs/evidence, prompt investigation and remediation, continuing updates, and appropriate contractual protection if facts develop. Make no unsupported conclusion about breach, harm, notification or quantum. | **Add investigation, preservation and update covenants and reserve rights** — current evidence is inconclusive, so neither dismissal nor an assumed liability amount is justified. |
| **SPA-N-013 Sandbar renewals** | Three AUD 110,000 renewals, AUD 330,000 total, characterised as ordinary-course operating costs. | Assess timing, scope, avoidability, termination rights, accrual and ordinary-course status; no automatic Debt treatment or price deduction. | **Reserve position pending diligence and funds-flow analysis** — the Seller’s ordinary-course label is not established by the disclosed material. |
| **SPA-N-014 Category separation** | Seller proposes limitations applying to all Claims unless expressly excluded, with exclusive-remedy/non-reliance provisions applying across all claim types. | Separate treatment for **Title/Fundamental, Tax, IP, payment obligations, indemnities and covenants**, without a hidden override by the general claims regime. | **Rewrite the limitation architecture with express category-specific rules** — an omnibus limitation could unintentionally cap or time-bar separately negotiated protections. |
| **SPA-N-015 Title verification** | Relies on the DD-012 internal share register as evidence that Seller owns 100% of the shares. | Independent evidence of ownership, title, encumbrance status, authority and valid transfer, including appropriate corporate searches, certificates/transfer documents and releases. | **Do not accept DD-012 as conclusive and require independent verification** — a company-maintained register is a supplied source, not independent proof of clean title. |
| **SPA-N-016 Tax/IP open terms** | Seller says Tax and IP warranties are “settled” under the proposed general regime. | Keep Tax and IP terms expressly **open**, separately negotiate their warranties, indemnities, caps and periods, and assume neither unlimited liability nor agreed resolution. | **Reject the claimed settlement and reserve all positions** — there is no Buyer authority or verified agreement supporting incorporation into the general regime. |
=== END ADVICE ===
